+import json
+from pathlib import Path
+
+import duckdb
+import matplotlib
+
+matplotlib.use("Agg")
+import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
+import pandas as pd
+
+
+OUT = Path("out")
+OUT.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
+df = duckdb.sql(
+    """
+    SELECT year(crash_date)::INTEGER AS year,
+           count(*)::BIGINT AS reported_crashes,
+           sum(number_of_motorist_killed)::BIGINT AS motorist_deaths,

+           count(*) FILTER (WHERE number_of_motorist_killed IS NULL) AS null_motorist_deaths
+    FROM read_parquet('data/crashes.parquet')
+    WHERE year(crash_date) BETWEEN 2013 AND 2025
+    GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1
+    """
+).df()
+df["motorist_deaths_per_100k_crashes"] = (
+    df["motorist_deaths"] / df["reported_crashes"] * 100_000
+)
+
+

+    ax.plot(df["year"], df[column], marker="o", linewidth=2.3, color="#176B87")

+    ax.tick_params(axis="x", rotation=45)
+    ax.set_ylabel(ylabel)
+    ax.set_xlabel("Crash year")
+    ax.set_title(title, loc="left", fontsize=14, weight="bold", pad=14)

+    ax.spines[["top", "right"]].set_visible(False)
+    for x, y in zip(df["year"], df[column]):
+        ax.annotate(fmt.format(y), (x, y), xytext=(0, 8), textcoords="offset points",
+                    ha="center", fontsize=8)
+    fig.text(0.01, 0.01, "Crash records do not include miles driven; this is not a per-mile risk rate.",
+             fontsize=9, color="#444444")

+    fig.savefig(OUT / filename, dpi=180, bbox_inches="tight")
+    plt.close(fig)
+
+
+df[["year", "motorist_deaths", "reported_crashes", "null_crash_date",
+    "null_motorist_deaths"]].to_csv(OUT / "values_1.csv", index=False)
+df[["year", "motorist_deaths", "reported_crashes",
+    "motorist_deaths_per_100k_crashes", "null_crash_date",
+    "null_motorist_deaths"]].to_csv(OUT / "values_2.csv", index=False)
+

+    "option_1.png", "motorist_deaths", "Motorist deaths (count)",
+    "Motorist deaths in police-reported NYC crashes, 2013–2025", "{:.0f}"
+)
+make_chart(
+    "option_2.png", "motorist_deaths_per_100k_crashes",
+    "Motorist deaths per 100,000 reported crashes",
+    "Motorist deaths per 100,000 police-reported crashes, 2013–2025", "{:.1f}"
+)
+
+start, end = df.iloc[0], df.iloc[-1]
+count_pct = (end.motorist_deaths / start.motorist_deaths - 1) * 100
+rate_pct = (end.motorist_deaths_per_100k_crashes /
+            start.motorist_deaths_per_100k_crashes - 1) * 100
+rows = []
+for row in df.itertuples():
+    rows.append({
+        "year": int(row.year),
+        "rows_in_year": int(row.reported_crashes),
+        "null_crash_date": int(row.null_crash_date),
+        "null_motorist_killed": int(row.null_motorist_deaths),
+    })
+assert all(r["null_crash_date"] == r["null_motorist_killed"] == 0 for r in rows)

+

+    "options": [
+        {
+            "id": 1,
+            "metric": "Annual number of motorist deaths in police-reported crashes",
+            "denominator": "None (annual total)",
+            "grouping": "Calendar year, 2013–2025",
+            "chart_type": "Line chart",
+            "reason": "Annual death counts show whether the total fatal burden went down, without implying an exposure-adjusted risk.",
+            "probability": 0.45,
+            "answer": f"Motorist deaths fell from {int(start.motorist_deaths)} in 2013 to {int(end.motorist_deaths)} in 2025 ({abs(count_pct):.1f}% lower), but this crash file cannot determine whether deaths per mile driven declined because it contains no miles-driven measure.",
+            "interpretation": f"This framing answers whether the annual count of motorists killed in reported NYC crashes declined: it fell from {int(start.motorist_deaths)} deaths in 2013 to {int(end.motorist_deaths)} in 2025, a {abs(count_pct):.1f}% decrease. An annual count is a defensible measure of fatal burden, but it is not a risk rate and can change with travel exposure. The question's per-mile-risk part remains unanswered because the file has no miles-driven denominator. Within 2013–2025, no rows are left out for NULL crash dates or motorist-killed values (0% in each year), and every included year is complete; other years are outside the requested period.",
+        },
+        {
+            "id": 2,
+            "metric": "Motorist deaths per 100,000 police-reported crashes",
+            "denominator": "All police-reported crash records in the same calendar year",
+            "grouping": "Calendar year, 2013–2025",
+            "chart_type": "Line chart",
+            "reason": "Normalizing deaths by reported crash volume distinguishes fatality burden from changes in the number of crashes, while remaining explicit about the available denominator.",
+            "probability": 0.55,
+            "answer": f"Motorist deaths per 100,000 reported crashes rose from {start.motorist_deaths_per_100k_crashes:.2f} in 2013 to {end.motorist_deaths_per_100k_crashes:.2f} in 2025 ({rate_pct:.1f}% higher), so this crash-based proxy did not decline; per-mile risk is not measurable from these data.",
+            "interpretation": f"This framing addresses a crash-normalized proxy for the requested risk: motorist deaths per 100,000 reported crashes increased from {start.motorist_deaths_per_100k_crashes:.2f} in 2013 to {end.motorist_deaths_per_100k_crashes:.2f} in 2025, up {rate_pct:.1f}%. It is defensible because the denominator controls for yearly police-reported crash volume, but it measures deaths relative to crashes rather than miles driven. Therefore the actual per-mile-risk question remains unanswered because no vehicle-miles-traveled or other miles-driven data are present. Within 2013–2025, no rows are left out for NULL crash dates, motorist-killed values, or crash-count denominators (0% in each year), and every included year is complete; other years are outside the requested period.",
+        },
+    ]
+}
+assert abs(sum(option["probability"] for option in options["options"]) - 1) < 1e-9
+(OUT / "options.json").write_text(json.dumps(options, indent=2) + "\n")
+
+print(df.to_string(index=False))
+print(f"2013–2025 count change: {count_pct:.2f}%")
+print(f"2013–2025 deaths per 100k crashes change: {rate_pct:.2f}%")
